subject: Subprocessor transition and UK addendum: routing & sign-off plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medivault.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Medivault Legal <legal@medivault.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: subprocessor swap + UK addendum evidence

Hi Ben,

Quick background: Medivault is preparing to swap one of our edge processors (EdgeTransit Ltd.) to a managed provider that will sit in the UK/EU footprint. Legal needs to confirm that the replacement provider will not create additional cross-border exposures under the UK IDTA / EU SCCs.

Can you share a concise list of the artifacts Redwood can deliver for the following items by next Friday?
- Confirmation of which subprocessors access plaintext data and the custody boundaries (redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v2.csv attached)
- Any TIA/DTIA evidence we can reuse for our UK addendum review (we attached our checklist to illustrate gaps)
- Proposed cutover window and rollback plan (we prefer end-of-month maintenance window)

We also need an updated statement on data residency routing and whether automatic fallback to a US-hosted variant could occur during capacity events — that affects our UK Addendum acceptance.

Attachments: medivault_tia_checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Compliance
Medivault Health
elena.rossi@medivault.com
Mobile: +44 7700 900123

Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor swap + UK addendum evidence

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. We'll put together a tight packet and a short transition plan. Quick notes:
- I pulled the latest subprocessor matrix (attached) — will validate the custody/access columns with infra.
- On fallback: our smart routing policy can fail over to US-hosted nodes only when explicit routing capacity tiers are exhausted; we can lock a geo-route for your tenant to prevent automatic fallback (that requires a DPA amendment).
- Cutover window: we can propose two maintenance windows (Nov 28-29 overnight UTC or Dec 5-6 overnight UTC) — both include a 2-hour planned window and a 4-hour verification period.

Can Laura and Logan pick up the evidentiary items? Kimberly, can you confirm whether the managed provider will require any key-handover or if we maintain KMS control?

Ben

Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor swap + UK addendum evidence

Team — looping legal/ops questions into one thread so we have a single source of truth. Action items below.

1) Evidence packet (what we'll deliver to Medivault):
   - DPA/UK Addendum excerpt highlighting routing lock capability (one-page summary)
   - TIA/DTIA artifacts: dataflow map, subprocessors list with access level (attested), encryption-at-rest/in-transit statements, SOC2 typology and last audit date
   - Operational controls: logging/traceability for the new provider, sample API call trace showing no plaintext persistence at the subprocessor

2) Technical clarifications needed from infra (assign to Logan):
   - Confirm whether KV cache replication crosses regions during autoscale bursts and, if so, whether it's encrypted and scrubbed.
   - Confirm KMS ownership model for the managed provider (Kimberly to confirm).

3) Proposed language for the UK Addendum: small routing clause that states Redwood will not perform automatic cross-border fallback for Medivault without prior written consent. If Medivault requires it codified, Legal will propose a DPA amendment.

Let's aim to have the draft packet ready by 2026-10-27 so Ben can share with Elena for their legal review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

From: logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor swap + UK addendum evidence

Laura/Ben — infra check completed. Key findings (summary):
- KV cache: replicated across pre-warmed edge nodes during high throughput events. Replication occurs within the EMEA-region by default; US-edge replication can only happen if you configure a multi-region pool and enable burst tiers. Medivault bucket is currently single-region (EU) in the staging tenant.
- Encryption: all in-transit links use TLS1.3; at-rest AES-256 with customer-seeded KMS available for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted tenants, Redwood-managed KMS is default.
- New managed provider: will not receive raw customer keys. We will broker access tokens; KMS keys remain in Redwood's control unless a customer requests a bring-your-own-key arrangement for Dedicated/Private.

Cutover/rollback proposal (concise):
- Planned window: 2026-11-28 00:00–02:00 UTC (primary) or 2026-12-05 00:00–02:00 UTC (alternate)
- Steps: preflight (30m), DNS & routing switch (15m), warm-up verification (45m), smoke tests (30m), monitoring (3h)
- Rollback: immediate DNS revert + traffic drain to prior provider; verify idempotency of caches and resync KV from snapshot (1h typical)

I attached the transition plan PDF (docsign_transition_plan.pdf). If Legal wants hard promises in the UK Addendum, we'll need to scope SLA/penalty language.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medivault.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Medivault Legal <legal@medivault.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor swap + UK addendum evidence — proposed packet and sign-off path

Elena — putting this across for your review. Attached is a compact evidence packet and an operational cutover plan. High-level summary below and next steps.

Summary of deliverables (attachments):
- redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v2.csv (detailed: access level + custody column)
- medivault_tia_checklist.xlsx (your original checklist, marked up with responses)
- docsign_transition_plan.pdf (detailed cutover/rollback, monitoring checkpoints)
- One-page routing-lock draft for inclusion in the UK Addendum (inline below)

Inline draft clause (for discussion):
"Redwood will not perform automatic cross-border fallback of Medivault tenant traffic outside the EU/UK without prior written consent from Medivault. In the event of an emergency capacity event, Redwood will notify Medivault within 15 minutes and will execute remediation steps to keep traffic within EU/UK regions where technically feasible. Any temporary cross-border fallback will be subject to the Data Processing Addendum amendment process and limited to the minimum scope necessary to mitigate service interruption."

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm which artifacts you need as certified copies vs. attestation (e.g., SOC2 cover letter vs. full report).
2) If the clause above is acceptable in principle, can Medivault Legal confirm whether they want the clause in the UK Addendum or a separate DPA amendment?
3) Pick preferred cutover window (Nov 28-29 or Dec 5-6) and we will open the change control ticket.

DocuSign: https://redwood.app/docusign/transition-plan-5678 (contains the cutover acknowledgement + routing-lock amendment if you elect the DPA path)

Thanks everyone — happy to jump on a quick call to walk Medivault through the packet.

Best,
Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
